Revealed tools: selecting upper-left 0/9 reveals a detailed icon; selecting upper-right 9 reveals a detailed icon. Early on, upper-center 2/8 and middle-center 3/2 seemed inert. Important navigation: up from the lower-center area can move to middle-center 3/2; left from there can move to a middle-left neutral room; left from the apparent upper-right active room transferred the active border onto upper-center. Major discovery: selecting middle-center 3/2 after both side tools were revealed caused a big mode/state change — the large top header band cleared, a small top-right marker changed, and the active border moved onto upper-center. In this new mode, repeated selects from the recent active room clearly alter the global top 14/8 header state. Important correction: the visible 11-border may be a column/room highlight rather than simply the upper-left tool itself. Critical failure note: moving down from the active upper neutral room during late header-cycling caused GAME_OVER, so avoid that move. After reset, selecting the starting room recreated the top-right 8 header band. Strong current hypothesis: repeated safe selects from the currently active 11-highlighted room drive a full 14→8 sweep; when the sweep finishes, the header resets and one small 8 marker pair turns into 3, indicating stage progress in a multi-stage sequence. Latest observation: after the previous reset, repeated selects have started another fresh sweep, with the top 14/8 boundary again expanding leftward from the far right while the small marker area still shows one 3-pair and two remaining 8-pairs. Safest current continuation remains repeated select until another reset, another 8→3 conversion, or a level transition occurs. Current likely active room appears to be the upper-center 11-highlighted room during this sweep. Extra pattern note: during this repeated-sweep phase, each select seems to move the top 14/8 boundary left by roughly a few columns while the upper-center room remains the visible 11-highlighted control. Latest immediate state: sweep still advances leftward without failure; maintain select spam unless the header resets, markers change, or a new room becomes clearly active. Step 180 still matches the same safe-sweep pattern, so continue selecting. Step 181 likewise continued the same sweep with no new conversion/reset, so continue select spam for now. Step 182 still appears to continue the same sweep with the top boundary moving farther left and no fresh 8→3 conversion visible. Step 183 also continues the same sweep pattern; keep selecting until a reset, marker conversion, or level transition occurs. Step 184/185 likewise continue the same sweep; top 14/8 boundary keeps moving left while only one small pair is converted to 3, so keep selecting. Current immediate state: the sweep has now pushed the 14/8 boundary deep into the left side without any visible second 8→3 conversion yet; still safest to continue selecting from the visible upper-center 11-highlighted control. Step 186/187 also continue the same sweep with no visible reset or second marker conversion, so keep selecting. Step 188/189 continue the same sweep; top boundary is now extremely far left, but still no visible second 8→3 conversion, so keep selecting until the next reset or state change. Step 190: only about six 14 cells remained at the far left of the top header. Step 191: only about three 14 cells remained. Step 192: full sweep completed; top header reset and a second small marker pair converted from 8 to 3. Now two 3-pairs and one final 8-pair remain. Post-step192 visible 11-highlight shifted onto the far-right upper room; with few turns left, test left from this room again to transfer highlight onto upper-center instead of continuing slow select-spam from far-right. New late-game probe: after transferring highlight onto upper-center, try down toward middle-center 3/2, because 3/2 previously triggered the major state change and may now finalize after two 3-pairs are complete. Distinguish this from the known-fatal down from an upper neutral room.

reasoning: Low turns remaining and directional probes have stalled. Best high-value attempt is a direct click on the middle-center 3/2 room, which previously caused the major mode/state change and may now finalize Level 1 after two small marker pairs have already converted to 3.
